approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a unique student identifier for people doing nationally recognised vocational education and training from 1 January 2015.
A Student Identifiers Registrar would assign, collect, use and disclose the identifier and maintain an authenticated transcript of each student's record.

The bill sets up a confidentiality scheme that prohibits collecting, using or disclosing identifiers without authorisation, except in prescribed circumstances, and requires destruction of personal information collected solely for the identifier application.
Introduces a student identifier for VET students.
Creates a Student Identifiers Registrar to administer the scheme.
Establishes an authenticated transcript of an individual's VET record.
Requires destruction of personal information collected only for the identifier application.
Makes unauthorised collection, use or disclosure of identifiers an interference with privacy under the Privacy Act 1988.
Requires the Registrar to protect records from misuse or unauthorised access.
Individuals undertaking nationally recognised vocational education and training, registered training organisations, and state, territory and Commonwealth governments.

Introduced the Student Identifiers Bill, creating a national lifelong unique student identifier for vocational education and training to reduce duplication, improve data accuracy, and give students online access to their training history from a single source.

Supported the Student Identifiers Bill, noting Labor had invested over $19 billion in skills funding between 2008 and 2013, a 77 per cent increase on the Howard government, and said the latest budget contained $2 billion in broken promises to the skills sector.

Supported the Student Identifiers Bill, establishing a unique student identifier for VET students, and outlined the government's Trade Support Loans of up to $20,000, repayable once apprentices earn around $50,000, with a 20 per cent discount for those who complete training.

Supported the Student Identifiers Bill but warned about declining training quality, citing Western Australia's TAFE fee for an 18-month nursing diploma rising from $2,000 to $8,000, and a resulting 4 per cent drop in the number of people in training.

Supported the Student Identifiers Bill and the government's $1.9 billion Trade Support Loans program, offering apprentices up to $20,000 across more than 1,000 eligible qualifications on the National Skills Needs List.

Supported the Student Identifiers Bill, saying Victoria University in his electorate has almost twice the national rate of first-in-family students at nearly 60 per cent, and blamed a $170 million Victorian state government cut to TAFE funding for the retrenchment of more than 13 student support workers there.

Summed up the Student Identifiers Bill, saying a review found the axed Australian Apprenticeships Access Program delivered only 26 per cent job outcomes, and that Labor's promise of trade training centres in all 2,650 secondary schools resulted in just 304 being built.
